answer: Each identity holds one lagoon inlet and locks a 65-credit bond. Each epoch it files one plume sample. The first filing costs 29 credits; the kth costs 29+8(k-1), so the 1,000th costs 8,021. Auditors recompute concentration from the lagoon dilution table and post each serial on the sonnet board; deviation over 3 percent, a reused serial, or one key filing twice burns the bond. Rented plume samples fail because each carries its owner's serial, so reuse shows as a duplicate. For 1,000 fakes fees total 4,025,000 plus 65,000 locked, while an honest identity pays 29 once, bond returned.
